LOCAL AND GENERAL.
Deptford Council are to destroy the captured German gun in Ravensbourne's Recreation Ground.
The Hongkong, Canton and Macno Steambout Co.'s steamer is to leave Macao on Sundays at 5 p.m. instead of 4 p.m.
The return of notifiable diseases in the Colony for the 24 hours ended April 29, shows one Chinese case of diphtheria.
Hearing the clinking. glasses, the owner of a house a Leicester descended to the wine cellar and disturbed burglars, who escaped.
Built during the war at a cost of over £200,000, the National Projectile Factory, Dudley, has been offered by the liquidation and Disposal Board to the local Chamber of Commerce for £60,000.

Canada, with an average wheat yield of 17.8 bushels over a period of twenty-three years, excels the United States, India, Russia, Argentina and Australia in production, according to E. S. Hopkins, Dominion Field Husbandman.

Two million years from now man will have a great brain, but he will be lacking in physical strength and ugly to look upon; says Professor Conrad Tharaldsen of the zoology department of Northwestern University.

The Shanghai Chinese General Chamber of Commerce has addressed a protest with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs against the establishment of savings societies by foreigners in the interior. The message urged that the existing societies under foreign control be required to put up sinking funds for their enterprises with reliable banks, which should be subject to the scrutiny of the Commissioner of Foreign Affairs and the competent consul.

A circular letter suggesting a presentation to H.E. the Governor (Sir R. E. Stubbs) by the Chinese community on the eve of his departure, was sent out yesterday by the Hon. Mr. R. H. Kotewall, the Chinese representative on the Legislative Council. A meeting is likely to be held shortly at the Chinese�'s Merchants' Club to discuss what form the presentation should take, as a tangible expression of the Chinese community's respect for His Excellency who will soon be leaving the Colony.
Mr. and Mrs. Tully (A. P. C.) leave for a holiday at Home tomorrow.

The Bishop of Manchester has accepted the invitation sent him by the students of the Y.M.C.A. and Y.W.C.A. associations to visit China next year, and an itinerary is being arranged for a series of visits to many centres in the country. The Bishop is spoken of as the possible next Archbishop of Canterbury.

The next fortnightly dances of the Peak Club will be held on May 9 and 23, starting on each occasion at 9.15 p.m.
Sure indication of the advent of spring is afforded by the work of the Floral Committee of the Canadian Pacific Railway. Thousands of packets of seeds are being distributed to all country stations along the three thousand miles of tracks. Between now and May very large numbers of trees, shrubs and other perennials will be shipped out, while at the end of May bedding plants will be sent out in hundreds of thousands. These will include allyssum, asters, cannas, coleus, geraniums, kochia, lobelia, marigolds, petunias, phlox, ricinus, sulvia, verbena, trailers, pansies.
SOCIAL AND PERSONAL.
Mr. W. A. Jordan who has contributed to the "China Mail's" correspondence columns on "Bible Fact" leaves the Colony for Home on Saturday next.

Among the passengers on the P. & O. Morea, which arrived from London yesterday were Mr. J. P. B. Eastwood (Jardine, Matheson & Co., Swatow) and Mrs. Eastwood; Mr. A. E. B. Lamble of the same branch of the Firm and Mrs. Lamble, Mr. R. B. Orr, of Messrs. Boyd & Co., Tamsul, and Mrs. Orr.

Mr. Oliver T. Breakspear, who was formerly manager of the Hongkong Daily Press. Ltd., and of the Publicity Bureau, returned to the Colony yesterday from London on the Morea, to succeed the late Mr. H. A. Cartwright as managing director of the Company. Mr. B. A. Hale, who has been recently in charge of the business, will shortly be proceeding. Homs on leave. Mrs. Hale is already on her way Home.

The Empire's Mother and Boy Competition closes on June 13, 1925, by which entries from overseas must reach London.
The silk shipped per s.s. President Madison, which sailed from Hongkong at 11 p.m., April 3, arrived New York at midnight on April 27, having been 24 days in transit.

Three gramophone records autographed by Paderewski and auctioned for the Polish White Cross were knocked down to Mr. H. H. Bowles, South Woodford, for £26.
The invention of the French engineer, M. André Citroën, of a type of motor car capable of crossing the hitherto formidable Sahara has produced a remarkable result. Timbuctoo, that mysterious place which even today some people think to be imaginary, has been brought within twelve days from London. The journey can now be made in perfect comfort, from the moment of leaving London in the ease of a Pullman to the final stage in a river motorboat from Gao to Timbuctoo on the Niger.

With 3,600,000 milch cows, 300,000 dairy farmers, 1,500 creameries and many thousand cheese factories, Canadians are the greatest butter eaters in the world, with an average annual per capita consumption in 1923 of 27.43 pounds, according to a statement of D'Arcy Scott. Secretary and Treasurer of the National Dairy Council of Canada.

Chinese suffragettes, who were prevented by the Shanghai Municipal Police from holding a mass meeting which they had planned for March 16 last in order to launch a campaign for women's representation at the Peking re-organisation conference, have filed a protest with the Municipal Council against police action in the matter.

The Issuance... of lottery tickets to aid the families of war victims has been authorised by General Chang Chung-chang, in command of the First Fengtien Army," according to advertisements in the Chinese Press.
... The Hon. Mr. Kotewall is to distribute the prizes at the Gap Road School on Tuesday next.

Chief Inspector J. E. Wheeler, who has been Acting Registrar at the Shanghai Mixed Court, was the recipient of a handsome cigarette and cigar box, on the eve of his departure for Home on leave, the presentation being made by Major F. L. Wainwright.

Mr. M. W. Pett, Chief Officer of the Shanghai Fire. Brigade, goes home shortly for a well-earned rest. Under his eggs, the Fire Brigade has been completely reorganized until it is now second to none in the Far East, and the benefits of the protective measures adopted by Mr. Pett are now accruing to the community.

A farewell luncheon was given at the American Club to Dr. Jacob Gould Schurman, former American Minister to Peking but now Ambassador-designate to Germany, by members of the American Association and the Chamber of Commerce. In the course of his address, Dr. Schurman said that he was greatly impressed by the friendliness subsisting between the Chinese and Americans, and urged everyone to stimulate and encourage that feeling to the utmost.

A farewell dinner was given to Mr. E. F. Mackay, retiring head of the firm of Butterfield and Swire, at the Union Club of China, Shanghai, by the Chinese members of the Club and friends. Eulogistic references were made by several speakers to Mr. Mackay's sterling qualities and his services to the community. Mr. Mackay has been the recipient of many valuable gifts from his Chinese friends, including some beautiful pieces of porcelain, bronze vases and urns, some said to be 2,000 years old. From the merchants connected with the Taikoo firm he has received a richly emblazoned scroll bearing some 100 signatures which will be a pleasant reminder of his sojourn in China.
Confronted with bound feet on all sides of him, the Tao-tai of Suiyuan, following a personal investigation of homes, has issued new instructions urging the magistrates to enforce the rules that the feet of women and girls must be unbound at once.

"Take less medicine and eat more fruit" is the slogan of the Leicestershire Health Insurance Committee, which is launching a campaign that will be carried out by means of cinema shows, posters, leaflets, and competitions, supported by lectures and gramophone recitals of special health songs in the schools. "The first principle of the Health Insurance Acts," said Mr. T. Crew, Clerk to the Committee, "is the prevention of sickness, and we are making a big effort to persuade the people of this country to return to natural health laws. The national drug bill under the Insurance Acts is far too high. If people would only rely more on fruit and other natural foods and remedies, they would be healthier and happier in every way."

A new Bible, based on the oldest Hebrew text available, and from which are eliminated references to wine familiar in the King James version, has been published by Charles Scribner's Sons. Issued in two volumes, the new version is known as the shorter Bible. The quotations in other versions of the Bible about David dealing out "a cake of bread and a good piece of flesh and a flagon of wine," appear in the shorter Bible as "a roll of bread, a portion of meat, and a cake of raisins." The prophet Isaiah's reference to the children of Israel looking to other gods and "loving flagons of wine" appears in the new Bible as "although they turned to other gods and loved to eat raisin cakes at their festivals."

Total value of all agricultural production, including game and furs, in Alberta during 1924 is estimated at $217,477,808, according to a report prepared by the Provincial Department of Agriculture. This is divided as follows: Grain crops, $106,699, -146: root and fodder crops, $54,393,675; other produce, including honey, wool, $267,642; dairy products, $22,928,750; poultry products, $8,916,000; animals slaughtered and sold, $20,772,593; game and furs, $2,000,000, and horticultural products, $1,500,000.
Mr. C. C. Hickling left yesterday by the St. Albums for Sydney.
Mr. Mrs. and Miss Hughes left for Melbourne yesterday by the St. Albums. Mr. and Mrs. J. R. Way are passengers by the same steamer.
Captain J. J. G. Patterson, who is to take over the command of H.M.A.S. Brisbane arrived in Hongkong by the Moren yesterday.
Mr. E. M. Moffatt and Mr. G. D. Meude arrived on the Morea yesterday to join the staff of the head office of the Hongkong and Shanghai Bank.
Viscount Fitzd�in has been appointed a Knight of the Order of the Garter, 'The Viscount has acted as Viceroy of Ireland and was also a Chief Unionist Whip.

Major Nathan, who is Chairman of the Kuilan Mining Administration in London and the Director of the Peking Syndicate, arrived in the Colony yesterday by the s.s. Morea. He is staying at the Hongkong Hotel, and will remain here for about a week. He then proposes to go North for the purpose of reviewing the position in connection with the two Sino-British Coal Companies.

Mrs. Jacob Gould Schurman, wife of the retiring American Minister to China, was entertained to tiffin by the American Women's Club in their rooms, when covers were laid for about 75 members and guests. The tiffin was in charge of the Social Committee, and its Chairman, Mrs. Lunt, acted as Mistress of Ceremonies. Among the guests who delivered impromptu speeches was Mrs. Lee Meriveather of St. Louis, Missouri, who, with her husband, a well-known author and lawyer, is visiting China. The Club's President, Dr. Anne W. Fearn, was, as usual, the afternoon's most effective speaker. Mrs. Schurman, in thanking the Club members for their hospitality on that and previous occasions, assured them that they would not be forgotten.
QUEEN'S THEATRE.
“THE COURTSHIP OF MYLES STANDISH.”

This film comes to the Queen's Theatre, to day, and local movie fans will find it filled with life and action, having a world of romance and thrilling adventure.
It is a big production, big in theme and big in cast, direction and expenditures, the building of the Mayflower alone costing $64,000.

When Charles May decided to produce his big film based upon Longfellow's famous poem it was distinctly understood that its making would be no rush job. Nine months of hard work, with more than $800,000 expended in the actual cost, has given the screen a tremendously important and finely-detailed production.

There is "mutiny at sea, with the Pilgrims' terrorized by an inhuman pirate crew that injects some thrilling climaxes into the story. The boat rides through one of the most sensational storms ever screened. Upon landing the colony is established and then comes fresh terrors, famine, disease and attacks by Indians. Through all the strife, trouble and days of tortuous anxiety the wonderful love of John Alden and Priscilla rides triumphant.

Charles Ray is John Alden and the screen has never seen a more gallant, more courageous and dashing young lover than he, fearing no danger that lurked, but ever bashful when in the presence of the beautiful maiden he loved.
Enid Bennett is Priscilla and her work could not be improved upon. She is sweet, comely and most natural in all her important love scenes with Ray.
MUSICAL CLOWNING.
SYMPHONY TO BE WRITTEN
"The red nose in music" is the title of a brief article in the Daily Mail, in which Sir Landon Ronald deplores the fact that a symphony is to be written in jazz.

So it has come to this, he laments. We are to have an entire symphony of jazz. First movement—slow movement—scherzo—with, I presume, a specially augmented orchestra and a strict sequence of symphonic form.

This is most depressing news. One had come to regard jazz as a necessary evil, because, to a certain extent, it reflects the age in which we live. But a whole symphony? It would be as bad as witnessing a long drama in which every character was a clown, or attending a banquet at which everybody present was a humorist.

For a symphony is, in many ways, as big a thing as a life, and some symphonies are very much bigger than some lives. And how can you write a whole life of jazz? The most you could do, I should imagine, would be to write a very short and rollicking movement, which might be taken as representative of second childhood.
For that is the only quality which jazz has added to music—the quality of low comedy. Humour, of course, music has always been able to express. Some of Chopin's Endes were witty as well as melodious, and the last movement of Beethoven's "Kreutzer Sonata" is an immense and breathless joke. But never before jazz has the goddess of music put on a red nose and borrowed the trappings of the clown.
